title: The Ass and His Shadow
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A certain man hired an Ass for a journey in summertime, and started out with the owner following behind to drive the beast. By and by, in the heat of the day, they stopped to rest, and the traveller wanted to lie down in the Ass's Shadow; but the owner, who himself wished to be out of the sun, wouldn't let him do that; for he said he had hired the Ass only, and not his Shadow: the other maintained that his bargain secured him complete control of the Ass for the time being. From words they came to blows; and while they were belabouring each other the Ass took to his heels and was soon out of sight.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why does the man hire the Ass?
options: To carry goods to a distant market
To help plow a field
For a journey in summertime
To race against other travellers

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who follows behind to drive the Ass?
options: The owner
A hired servant
The traveller's son
A passing stranger

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where does the traveller want to lie down when they stop to rest?
options: Beneath a nearby tree
Inside a roadside inn
On the Ass's back
In the Ass's Shadow

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why does the owner refuse to let the traveller use the shadow?
options: He believed the shadow belonged to someone else
He himself wished to be out of the sun
He thought the Ass needed the shade to rest
He wanted to charge an extra fee for its use

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the owner say his bargain with the traveller covered?
options: The Ass and everything it carried
The Ass for the entire summer season
The Ass only, and not his Shadow
The Ass, but only for half of the journey

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Ass do while the two men are fighting?
options: He takes to his heels and is soon out of sight
He lies down calmly between them
He kicks at both men to stop the fight
He wanders back toward his owner's home

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the traveller believe he has a right to the shadow as well as the Ass?
options: He believes the owner promised him the shadow separately
He believes the shadow belongs to whoever reaches it first
He believes the owner no longer has any claim on the Ass
He believes hiring the Ass gives him complete control over everything connected to it

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what is ironic about the outcome of the two men's argument?
options: The Ass turns out to belong to neither of them
While they fight over the Ass, they lose the Ass itself entirely
The shadow disappears before either man can use it
The argument is settled peacefully in the end

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that the men "came to blows"?
options: They agreed to end their argument peacefully
They asked a judge to settle their dispute
They began physically fighting each other
They decided to share the shadow equally

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Arguing over a minor gain can cause you to lose something far more valuable
Hired animals always belong entirely to whoever pays for them
Shadows are more valuable than the animals that cast them
Travelling in summer is always more dangerous than in other seasons

questions.prompt: According to the passage, when do the two men stop to rest?
options: Early in the morning
Just before nightfall
During a sudden rainstorm
In the heat of the day

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the owner want just as much as the traveller does?
options: To finish the journey quickly
To be out of the sun
To be paid more money
To rest inside a nearby building

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the disagreement between the two men begin?
options: With a sudden physical fight, with no words first
With the owner walking away silently
With words, before turning into blows
With the Ass refusing to move at all

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does neither man notice the Ass slipping away?
options: They are too absorbed in fighting each other to pay attention to it
The Ass is tied up securely the whole time
The Ass moves too slowly to be noticed leaving
A third person distracts them at the same moment

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the dispute over the shadow reveal about how the men value the actual point of their bargain?
options: They both agree the shadow matters more than the Ass
They both realize the argument is pointless from the start
They both believe the Ass is not worth arguing over at all
They lose sight of the Ass itself while quarreling over a lesser, secondary claim

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "belabouring" mean in "while they were belabouring each other"?
options: Speaking calmly
Striking repeatedly
Walking slowly
Resting quietly

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: Two men share the Ass's shadow peacefully during their rest
An Ass refuses to continue the journey in the summer heat
Two men fight over an Ass's shadow and lose the Ass itself in the process
A traveller returns the Ass to its owner before the journey ends
